title: omicstra: a multi-agent MCP server for cross-modal embedding alignment and evidence-based routing in spatial biology
description:
A multi-agent MCP server for spatial biology. Modality-specialized agents and their integration are orchestrated with LangGraph; foundation-model encoders are pluggable; integration strategy is a configurable experimental dimension. Alignments are evaluated against declared metrics, and questions are routed from a cohort's own recorded evidence, refusing when that evidence is absent rather than inheriting another cohort's result. Agents are deterministic components with persistent context; the server ships no model.

This is a pre-release of v1.1. v1.0 ships the read path - inventory, EDA, admissibility gate and routing - over stdio and HTTP, with the seed cohort's evidence pack committed so a fresh clone can route without training anything. This snapshot adds the compute-path groundwork: a canonical cohort ingest, the Virchow2 encoder port verified against the cached embeddings that produced the published grid, the compute contract's preflight gates, and a shard dispatcher that resumes after a kill. omicstra run - the end-to-end command that defines v1.1 - is not yet built.

creators.name: Sanati, Nasim
creators.affiliation: Sears Lab, Brenden-Colson Center, OHSU Knight Cancer Institute

notes: Funded by the ResearchHub Foundation (doi:10.55277/researchhub.6ou1w3h3). Seed cohort: 92 triple-negative breast cancer patients from Wang et al. 2024, Nature Communications 15:10232 - original Spatial Transcriptomics platform, co-registered with H&E whole-slide images. The package ships no cohort data; it is pointed at a cohort directory.
